ideas: What made you decide to change
How you started and what was difficult

phrases.meaning: an event that shows you must change
a life with little physical activity

model: A healthy change I made was starting to run regularly, which I've been doing for about eighteen months now. Before that, I had quite a sedentary lifestyle. I sat at a desk all day, I took a motorbike everywhere, and I hardly ever exercised. The real wake-up call came at a company health check, when the doctor told me my blood pressure was a bit high for my age and said I should do at least thirty minutes of exercise a few times a week. She also said I ought to cut down on sugary coffee, which was harder to hear, to be honest. So I decided to get into shape. At first, I was out of breath after running for just five minutes around the park near my flat, and it was quite embarrassing. A friend who's a keen runner told me I had to build up gradually rather than trying to do too much, so I followed a beginner's plan on my phone. There were plenty of mornings when I didn't want to get up, but I made myself stick with it. Now I run three times a week, and last spring I finished my first ten-kilometre race. It's really made a difference. I sleep better, I feel more energetic at work, and my blood pressure is back to normal. My only rule now is that I'd better not skip more than two sessions in a row, or I lose my motivation.
